claims.text: Adding a refractory element improves the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy.
Tungsten or molybdenum can be used as the refractory-element intervention.
The refractory element should be added at 5–10 at%.
The intervention is applicable above 500 °C under high stress.
The refractory-element addition causes formation of a stable precipitate phase.
The refractory-element addition causes formation of a coherent precipitate phase.
The refractory-element-induced microstructure pins grain boundaries.
The refractory-element addition improves yield strength relative to the alloy without the addition.
The refractory-element addition improves creep resistance relative to the alloy without the addition.
The proposed composition range is 20–40 at% Ti, 20–40 at% Ni, and 5–10 at% refractory element.
The proposed operating window is 500–1000 °C and 100–500 MPa.
Yield strength and creep strain can be compared between otherwise matched alloys with and without the refractory-element addition.
TEM and XRD can be used to examine the proposed microstructural mediator.
The hypothesis is falsified if the modified alloy shows no significant improvement in yield strength or creep resistance over the unmodified alloy.

contradictions.description: The material is designated a high-entropy alloy subject to the stated 5–35 at% per-element definition, but the boundary permits Ti or Ni concentrations as high as 40 at%.
The conditions specify temperatures above 500 °C, whereas the boundary includes 500 °C itself.
